About[6 in 10 Americans live within 2 miles of an electric vehicle public charging station](https://www.pewresearch.org/data-labs/2024/05/23/electric-vehicle-charging-infrastructure-in-the-u-s/#:~:text=for%20geographic%20data-,64%25%20of%20Americans%20live%20within%202%20miles%20of%20a%20public,chargers%20view%20EVs%20more%20positively&text=Pew%20Research%20Center%20conducted%20this,30%20to%20June%204%2C%202023.) , according to the Pew Research Center. And as of October 2026, there are over 80,000 public charging stations across the U.S.


[Electric vehicle (EV)](https://www.wexinc.com/resources/blog/ev-everything-you-need-to-know-for-your-commercial-vehicle-fleet/) charging accessibility is growing, pushing the EV transition within reach for many businesses.


For fleet managers, electric vehicles present a unique opportunity to reduce emissions, lower operational costs, and contribute to a sustainable future. However, one of the primary challenges that comes with this transition is the accessibility of charging stations while on the go, especially during long routes.


This is where services, such as[WEX’s EV En Route](https://www.automotive-fleet.com/10220084/wex-rolls-out-ev-fleet-management-solutions#:~:text=WEX%20En%20Route%20is%20an%20EV%20public%20charging%20payment%20and%20reporting%20system.&text=%E2%80%9CWEX%20services%20approximately%20600%2C000%20commercial,a%20unique%20set%20of%20variables.) tool, come into play, offering comprehensive electric vehicle charging, payment, and management solutions that help keep your commercial vehicles powered and operational on the road. WEX EV En Route simplifies public charging through innovative payment and reporting functions giving managers clear insights into driver behavior, charging patterns, and more.


## **Electric vehicle charging infrastructure in the U.S.**


In 2020, the Department of Energy reported[nearly 29,000 public charging stations nationwide](https://afdc.energy.gov/data/10972) . As of October 2026, that number has multiplied to 80,000. For reference, there are currently around[145,000 traditional fueling stations nationwide.](https://www.pewresearch.org/data-labs/2024/05/23/electric-vehicle-charging-infrastructure-in-the-u-s/#:~:text=For%20reference%2C%20there%20are%20an%20estimated%20145%2C000%20gasoline%20fueling%20stations%20in%20the%20country.)


According to the Pew Research Center, the majority of EV charging stations are located around major hub cities. As of[September of 2025,](https://www.energy.ca.gov/news/2025-09/california-exceeds-200000-electric-vehicle-chargers) California has 201,180 public chargers. New York has the second most with 17,663 public charging stations.


EV charging stations are located in two-thirds of all U.S. counties, which include 95% of the U.S. population.


## **Types of electric vehicle chargers**


The U.S Department of Transportation lists three types of EV chargers:


[Level 1, 2, and 3 (DC fast chargers)](https://www.transportation.gov/rural/ev/toolkit/ev-basics/charging-speeds)


- **Level 1 chargers** refer to private home chargers. Those use a lower voltage and typically take longer to charge. They can take 40-50+ hours to charge a BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle) to 80 percent from empty and 5-6 hours for a PHEV (Plug-In Hybrid Electric Vehicle).


- **Level 2 chargers** can charge a BEV to 80 percent from empty in 4-10 hours and a PHEV in 1-2 hours.


- **Level 3 (DC) chargers** can charge a BEV to 80 percent in just 20 minutes to 1 hour.


[According to Bloomberg, the U.S. government is investing in the development of EV infrastructure](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-04-18/the-us-now-has-a-fast-ev-charging-station-for-every-15-gas-stations) to eliminate charging hurdles. The National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure program – a $5 billion plan to address gaps in charging availability – has helped add more Level 3 fast chargers to the landscape. During the first quarter of 2024, public fast-charging stations in the U.S. increased by 7.6%, bringing the total number to 8,200 nationwide.


## **WEX EV En Route simplifies on-the-go charging**


WEX EV En Route offers a range of features that simplify the complexities of public charging:


### **Enhancement of the driver experience**


To access WEX’s public charging network, drivers can use the[DriverDash app](https://www.wexinc.com/products/fuel-cards-fleet/fleet-mobile-apps/#:~:text=their%20refueling%20stops.-,DriverDash,-DriverDash%3A%20A) – a user-friendly app that simplifies the charging or fueling process – or the WEX EV RFID card. DriverDash, which can also be used by drivers of gas-powered vehicles to find and pay for gas, provides real-time information on and directions to nearby available charging stations, and allows drivers to initiate a charging session.


### **Secure payment network**


With the DriverDash app **** and RFID card, WEX EV En Route uses WEX’s proprietary closed-loop payments network to help ensure secure transactions and provide fleet managers with detailed insights into charging behavior, driver identification, and vehicle mileage.


DriverDash is accepted at a growing network of accepting charging locations, including ChargePoint, EVConnect, EVGo, FLO, AmpUp, and Blink.


### **Optimized route planning**


Managers should take into account the locations of charging stations, estimated charging times, and the specific range capabilities of each EV in their commercial vehicle fleet. Using the DriverDash app helps drivers avoid running out of power mid-route. This enhances vehicle reliability and reduces the risk of disruptions in the workday.


### **Simplified cost management and billing**


Cost management with EV charging can be complex, but WEX EV En Route simplifies the process of managing a mixed-energy fleet, with one credit line, one invoice, and one set of reports for all of your charging and fuel purchases. It also provides insights into charging costs across different stations and times, allowing managers to strategically pick stations for cost and time efficiency.


Learn more on how WEX EV En Route can benefit your fleet.
